messages:
Sam (CS): Priya from NovaPayments just pinged — they say after our 03/10 latency-optimized rollout their invoices assistant is hallucinating account numbers and inventing bank names. They claim it was fine before the rollout. :warning:
Priya (Customer): Hi team — we updated to your hosted endpoint yesterday. Previously when we asked 'what bank issued account x' the model returned 'Chase' (correct based on our training set). Now it returns 'Northbridge Savings' (not a real bank in our data). This is causing PII redaction failures on our side.
Marta (support): Oof. Are they using a pinned model version or the default route? Any error codes in logs?
Priya (Customer): We're calling `/v1/generate` with model `redwood-text-3.4-latopt` (that's what console shows as active for our org). No API errors, just wrong text in outputs. Calls have `temperature:0.0`, `top_p:1.0`. We can share a repro curl.
Sam (CS): Please paste one reproducible request + response. We need quick repro to show eng.
Priya (Customer): Here — repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-text-3.4-latopt","input":"Which bank issued account 8432-XXXX?","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":60}'
```
Response (trimmed):
```json
{"id":"gen_abc","output":"Northbridge Savings issued this account on 2018-06-11. Contact: support@northbridge.example"}
```
Expected: short answer referencing internal mapping or a fallback 'I don't have that info'.
Riley (eng-runtime): Thanks — givens look solid. DeployBot shows `deploy redwood-text-3.4-latopt -> 2026-03-10T22:40Z` and rollout to 100% on 2026-03-11. Canary was 15% for ~3 hours.
DeployBot: deploy redwood-text-3.4-latopt succeeded (canary 15% -> global 100%).
Luca (eng-ml): Quick hypothesis: we applied a new prompt-template optimization that strips system guard rails in some low-entropy / short-context cases to squeeze latency. That could remove the explicit 'no hallucination' system prompt. Can you confirm what system messages were sent?
Marta (support): Priya confirms they do not send an app-level system prompt. They relied on model behavior before.
Sam (CS): Can eng-ml run a diff eval between previous stable (`redwood-text-3.3-stable`) and `3.4-latopt` on the customer's prompt set? Also check any change to safety/system prompt or default `temperature` handling.
Luca (eng-ml): On it. Initial quick check: the latency build used an internal micro-prompt merge which mistakenly omits the default safety wrapper for zero-shot Q/A under token budget. I'll run a 1k-prompt regression on their sample set and post numbers.
Riley (eng-runtime): Also please check caching/prefix-kv changes — if we started using prefix caching aggressively, stale cached completions could be injected. Any chance of cross-request bleed?
Luca (eng-ml): Not likely but I'll audit KV cache keys for canary timeline.
Marta (support): Priya — we will rollback your org to `redwood-text-3.3-stable` for now while we investigate. Do you want us to do that immediately?
Priya (Customer): Yes please. This is causing false positives in our redaction pipeline, blocking our batch job. Appreciate the fast action.
Sam (CS): Action items: (1) Marta to rollback customer to 3.3 (done within 30m). (2) Luca to run automated regression + share diff (precision/recall on factuality tests). (3) Riley to audit deploy config for prompt wrapper & cache keys. (4) Eng to prepare a short postmortem and fix and then a targeted canary with extra evals.
Luca (eng-ml): Initial regression (first 200 prompts) — 3.3 factuality score 98.2%, 3.4-latopt 82.4%. Big gap on short direct fact lookups. I'll attach full CSV to the ticket (link to follow).
Riley (eng-runtime): Found the prompt wrapper flag `--omit-default-system` was flipped in the latency pipeline by accident in PR #1246. That explains it. Reverting now for future canaries.
Sam (CS): Thanks — keep this thread updated. We'll send Priya a summary once rollback is confirmed and include ETA for permanent fix. Priya, sorry for the disruption — we'll prioritize. :bow:
